name: Mars
blurb: MOLA topography and the GMM-3 gravity field. Drawn from the Mars Planetary Modeling Atlas.

grids.label: Topography
grids.note: MOLA laser altimetry, height above the areoid. From the floor of Hellas to the top of Olympus Mons is about 30 km.

grids.label: Free-air gravity
grids.note: GMM-3 (Genova et al. 2016) at 3396 km, degrees 2–120 with a taper above 80, with the rotational flattening (C20) removed. The Tharsis volcanoes and Olympus Mons are the strongest highs.

grids.label: Bouguer gravity
grids.note: Free-air minus the pull of the MOLA shape (ρ = 2900 kg/m³). Highs under Hellas, Isidis and Utopia mark thin crust; lows under Tharsis and the southern highlands mark thick crust.

grids.label: Areoid
grids.note: The Mars geoid from GMM-3, height above its best-fit ellipsoid. Tharsis loads the whole planet into a bulge.

sites.name: Viking 1
sites.note: Chryse Planitia; first successful Mars landing with surface science, 2,245 sols.

sites.name: Sojourner (Pathfinder)
sites.note: Ares Vallis; first rover on Mars.

sites.name: Opportunity
sites.note: Meridiani Planum; 5,111 sols and about 45 km driven.

sites.name: Phoenix
sites.note: Vastitas Borealis; dug up water ice just below the surface.

sites.name: InSight
sites.note: Elysium Planitia; seismometer that recorded more than 1,300 marsquakes.

sites.name: Perseverance
sites.note: Jezero crater delta; caching samples. Ingenuity flew from here.

sites.name: Beagle 2
sites.note: Isidis Planitia; landed but its solar panels did not fully open.

sites.name: Mars 3
sites.note: Terra Sirenum (estimated); transmitted for about 20 s after landing.

sites.name: Mars 2
sites.note: Crashed during descent; first object on Mars (position estimated).

sites.name: Mars 6
sites.note: Margaritifer Terra; contact lost just before touchdown (estimated).

sites.name: Mars Polar Lander
sites.note: Ultimi Scopuli (target area); lost during descent.

sites.name: Schiaparelli
sites.note: Meridiani Planum; crashed after a software error during descent.

sources: Smith et al. (2001), MOLA, as gridded in the Mars Planetary Modeling Atlas
Genova et al. (2016), GMM-3 gravity field (SHTOOLS example file gmm3_120_sha.tab)
